title: UNIT 3: MOTION IN A STRAIGHT LINE
notes:
✓ Motion → Continuous change in position of an object with time relative to a reference frame.

✓ Motion in a straight line → Rectilinear or one-dimensional motion.

title: 3.1 POSITION, DISTANCE AND DISPLACEMENT
notes:
✓ Reference frame → Set of coordinates used to determine the position of an object.

✓ Position → Location of an object relative to a reference point or origin.

✓ Distance → Total path length travelled; it is a scalar quantity.

✓ Displacement → Change in position from initial to final position in a specific direction; it is a vector quantity.

✓ Distance → Is always positive, while displacement can be positive, negative or zero.

title: 3.2 AVERAGE SPEED AND INSTANTANEOUS SPEED
notes:
✓ Speed → Rate at which distance is covered; it is a scalar quantity.

◆ AVERAGE SPEED
✓ Average speed = Total distance / Total time

vₐᵥ = sₜₒₜ / tₜₒₜ

✓ Instantaneous speed → Speed of an object at a particular instant.

✓ Speedometer → Measures instantaneous speed.

✓ SI unit of speed → m/s.
✓ Other unit → km/h.

title: 3.3 AVERAGE VELOCITY AND INSTANTANEOUS VELOCITY
notes:
✓ Velocity → Rate of change of displacement; it is a vector quantity and includes direction.

◆ AVERAGE VELOCITY
✓ Average velocity = Displacement / Time

v⃗ₐᵥ = Δx⃗ / Δt

✓ Instantaneous velocity → Velocity of a body at a specific instant.

✓ SI unit → m/s.

✓ Constant velocity → Average velocity = instantaneous velocity.

title: 3.4 ACCELERATION
notes:
✓ Acceleration → Rate of change of velocity with time.

◆ AVERAGE ACCELERATION
ā = (v⃗f − v⃗i) / Δt

✓ SI unit → m/s².

✓ Positive acceleration → Velocity increases in the chosen positive direction.
✓ Negative acceleration/deceleration → Velocity decreases.

✓ Acceleration → Can occur when an object speeds up, slows down or changes direction.

title: 3.5 UNIFORM MOTION
notes:
✓ Uniform motion → Motion along a straight line with constant velocity or speed in a given direction.

◆ PROPERTIES
✓ Equal distances → Are covered in equal time intervals.
✓ Velocity → Remains constant.
✓ Acceleration → 0.
✓ Average velocity → Instantaneous velocity.

✓ Example → A car moving on a straight road at constant speed.

title: 3.6 GRAPHICAL REPRESENTATION OF MOTION
notes:
✓ Motion → Can be represented using graphs to show how position, distance, speed or velocity changes with time.

◆ POSITION/DISTANCE-TIME (s-t) GRAPH
✓ Slope → Gives speed or velocity depending on the quantity plotted.
✓ Horizontal line → Object is at rest.
✓ Straight sloping line → Constant speed/velocity.

◆ VELOCITY-TIME (v-t) GRAPH
✓ Slope → Acceleration.
✓ Horizontal line → Constant velocity and zero acceleration.
✓ Area under a velocity-time graph → Displacement.

✓ Position-time graph slope at a specific time → Instantaneous velocity.

title: SPEED LIMIT AND TRAFFIC SAFETY
notes:
✓ Speed limits → Specify the maximum permitted speed of vehicles.

✓ High speed → Increases the risk and severity of accidents because vehicles become harder to control.

✓ Speedometer → Measures instantaneous speed.

✓ Maintaining a safe speed → Helps protect people, animals and property.

title: UNIT 3 — MUST REMEMBER
notes:
◆ MOTION
✓ Change in position with time relative to a reference frame.

◆ DISTANCE
✓ Total path length → Scalar.

◆ DISPLACEMENT
✓ Change in position + direction → Vector.

◆ AVERAGE SPEED
✓ Total distance / Total time.

◆ AVERAGE VELOCITY
✓ Displacement / Total time.

◆ ACCELERATION
✓ Change in velocity / Time.

◆ UNITS
✓ Distance/Displacement → m.
✓ Speed/Velocity → m/s.
✓ Acceleration → m/s².

◆ GRAPHS
✓ Position-time slope → Velocity.
✓ Velocity-time slope → Acceleration.
✓ Velocity-time area → Displacement.

◆ EXAM TIP
✓ Distance and speed → Do not require direction.
✓ Displacement and velocity → Require direction.
